entities.paper: Tackling Online Abuse: A Survey of Automated Abuse Detection Methods

feature_sets_nobata.text: Nobata et al. evaluated a large range of features on the Yahoo! datasets using a regression model: (1) word and character n-grams; (2) linguistic features such as number of polite/hate words and punctuation count; (3) syntactic features such as parent and grandparent of a node in a dependency tree; (4) distributional-semantic features such as paragraph2vec comment representations.

char_ngram_robustness.text: Although the best results were achieved with all features combined, character n-grams on their own contributed significantly more than other features due to their robustness to noise (obfuscations, misspellings, unseen words).

char_vs_word_superiority.text: Mehdad and Tetreault's results demonstrated the superiority of character-level features over word-level ones, with SVM classifiers trained on Bayesian log-ratio vectors of average counts of character n-grams outperforming the approach of Nobata et al. in terms of AUC as well as other RNN-based character and word-level models.

bow_features.text: Bag-of-words (BOW) features have been integral to several works on abuse detection; for example, Sood et al. showed that an SVM trained on word bi-gram features outperformed a word-list baseline using a Levenshtein distance-based heuristic for detecting profanity.

word_ngrams_other_features.text: Word n-grams have been used in conjunction with other features, such as typed-dependency relations or scores based on sentiment lexicons, to train SVMs.

tfidf_ngrams.text: Salminen et al. showed that a linear SVM using tf-idf weighted n-grams achieves the best performance on classification of hateful comments as one of 29 different hate categories.

hand_engineered_features.text: Samghabadi et al. augmented features with hand-engineered ones such as polarity scores derived from SentiWordNet, measures based on the LIWC program, and features based on emoticons; distributional-semantic features combined with these constituted an effective feature space.

char_ngrams_general.text: In line with the findings of Nobata et al. and Mehdad and Tetreault, character n-grams performed well on the datasets used by Samghabadi et al.

germeval_winning.text: The winning system of the GermEval shared task employed multiple character and token n-gram classifiers, as well as distributional semantic features obtained by averaging word embeddings.

hindi_lexical.text: The top approach for Hindi in the aggression identification shared task utilized lexical features based on word and character n-grams.

sarcasm_surface_insufficient.text: Sarcastic comments are hard for abuse detection methods to deal with since surface features are not sufficient; typically knowledge of the context or background of the user is also required.

metaphor_frequency.text: Mishra found that metaphors are more frequent in abusive samples as opposed to non-abusive ones.
